---
title: "Pre-processing workflow"
description: "Prepare quantitative proteomics data for QC and differential abundance analysis."
---

## Recommended order

ProtVis separates preprocessing into four explicit modules:

**Correct Noise → Data Transformation → Data Imputation → Data Normalization**

Keeping these decisions separate makes it easier to inspect the effect of each operation and to record the selected method in the project history.

## 1. Correct noise

The current noise-correction logic is replicate-aware. For sample groups whose names contain replicate suffixes such as `_1`, `_2`, and `_3`, zero/missing cells are corrected only when sufficient non-zero replicate evidence exists; otherwise the affected replicate group remains missing. Duplicate protein IDs are collapsed safely before reshaping to avoid accidental many-to-many expansion.

Read [Correct noise](correct_noise.qmd).

## 2. Data transformation

ProtVis currently exposes **None, log10, log2, Standardization, Z-Score, scale, center, and scale-center**. Original and transformed distributions can be compared before proceeding.

Read [Data transformation](data_transformed.qmd).

## 3. Data imputation

Missing measurements are visualized before imputation. The current GUI offers **kNN, RF, Mean, Median, Zero, and Minimum**, with **kNN** selected by default. Legacy missing sentinels such as `0` and `-8` are kept as true `NA` until the user runs imputation.

Read [Data imputation](data_imputation.qmd).

## 4. Data normalization

The current normalization module performs **column-wise median subtraction**, centering each sample by its median. Original and normalized boxplots can be compared and downloaded.

Read [Data normalization](data_normalization.qmd).

## Stage outputs

The canonical result after each step is a new `ProtVis_dataset` state. Compatibility stage files are also used by the GUI:

| Stage | Compatibility file |
|---|---|
| Correct noise | `Step3_correct_noise.rda` |
| Transformation | `Step4_data_transformed.rda` |
| Imputation | `Step5_data_imputation.rda` |
| Normalization | `Step6_data_normalization.rda` |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Do not impute before inspecting missingness
Missing values in proteomics are not always random. Use the missing-value visualization and the biological design to decide whether a global imputation strategy is appropriate for your experiment.
:::

## What to check before downstream analysis

Before opening **Overview** or **DEP analysis**, verify that sample names match `sample_info`, no sample is unexpectedly all missing, transformed values are on the intended scale, imputation did not create implausible distributions, and normalization reduced unwanted sample-level shifts without erasing known biological differences.
